title: Uninvestment Check
concept: A short, honest count to tell needing space (still invested) apart from pulling away — so you know which repair to reach for. It describes behaviour you can both see, never your partner’s intent.
whenToUse: When warmth is missing even in ordinary moments, repairs feel like going through the motions, you’ve stopped planning ahead together, or contempt has replaced frustration.
steps: Each of you marks, on your own, which of the eight signs (listed under Practise) you’ve noticed, then share. Describe behaviour you’ve seen — don’t claim to know the other person’s intent.
If contempt is one of your signs, skip the count: contempt means stop and get outside support first. The same goes for fear or coercion at any count.
None of these? You’re fine. Keep up the daily floor. 1–2 signs → likely needs space and small repairs (Micro-Repair, Morning + Evening Rhythm).

3 or more signs → may be pulling away. Book a Full Recovery conversation within a week. For drift, no one “caused” it: you both name your part. (A specific breach of trust goes to Trust Recovery instead.)
Set a time window to check whether you’re both leaning back in.

phrases.text: I’m noticing some distance. Do you just need space, or is something bigger going on?
I want a Full Recovery conversation. Can we book it for when we’re both calm?
Contempt means we can’t just carry on as normal.

working: A marks three signs, B marks four: fewer messages, only logistics, repairs on autopilot. They book a Full Recovery conversation within a week, then keep up their morning and evening check-ins for 21 days, looking back once a week.
notWorking: One of you waits for the other “to miss me”. Weeks go by with nothing booked, and the quiet starts to feel normal.
activity: Fill in the Uninvestment Check Worksheet separately, then compare counts. Check monthly, or weekly if you’re worried. The eight signs — each of you marks, on your own: (1) fewer non-logistical check-ins, (2) less curiosity about each other, (3) avoiding future plans, (4) doing more on your own in place of shared time (time apart is healthy), (5) mostly practical conversations, (6) going-through-the-motions affection, (7) repairs that feel routine, (8) contempt instead of frustration. Then count them; contempt never goes into the count (see step 2). None of these? You’re fine. Keep up the daily floor. 1–2: likely needs space and small repairs. 3 or more: may be pulling away — book a Full Recovery conversation within a week.
warn: If contempt is one of your signs, skip the count: contempt means stop and get outside support first. Fear or coercion at any count: stop; safety and outside support come first.
note: Deciding not to rebuild, or to end the relationship, is a valid outcome of this protocol, not a failure of it.
